correctness.rationale: Translating the site p to zero gives g(y)=yᵀHy+2bᵀy−c, with H=A−B, b=B(q−p), c=(q−p)ᵀb>0, g(0)<0 and g(q−p)>0. A positive semidefinite H makes the closed sublevel set convex and hence site-star. Otherwise, on each negative quadratic direction both sufficiently remote signed endpoints lie in the cell, so site-star visibility would force the entire line into the cell. On any limit null direction its linear coefficient must vanish. For indefinite H the null directions span the space by pairing positive and negative eigenvectors (and including the kernel), forcing b=0 contrary to c>0. For nonzero negative semidefinite H every direction is a limit of negative directions, including q−p, so continuity would give g(q−p)≤0. This also covers dimension one. The witnesses produced by failure of site-star visibility have a positive gap on an eventual-inside ray, consistent with the stated quadratic roots. Interchanging the sites gives both cells site-star exactly when H and −H are both positive semidefinite, i.e. A=B.
residual_risks: Independent hand substitution for the supplied ray yields g(tu)=−21t²+20t−1, with values −1, 15/4 and −2 at t=0, 1/2 and 1. This certifies one non-star example, not the universal theorem. No Lean or expert attestation claimed.

evidence: The tensor formulas of Venkovic–Anzt are for cells already star-convex at their site. Labelle–Shewchuk treat wedge-restricted two-site visibility and give wedging as a sufficient condition. Cañas–Gortler give sufficient orphan-freeness conditions. Held–de Lorenzo's inspected passages give a computational framework for scalar multiplicative weights.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The assumptions and conclusions differ: a conditional tensor formula does not determine when its hypothesis holds. Sufficient sampling or face-wedging conditions for a broader diagram class do not logically give an unrestricted matrix-order iff for an arbitrary pair. Scalar multiplicative metrics restrict the two matrices to scalar multiples of the identity and omit indefinite differences.

evidence: For p=0, q=e₁, A=2I, B=I in the plane, the full cell is the disk (x₁+1)²+x₂²≤2, star at 0, but the bisector exits the wedge 0<x₁<1. Thus the cited face-wedging hypothesis is not necessary in this setting.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Convexity from positive semidefiniteness is standard; the new direction uses the generating-site constraints c>0 and g(q−p)>0 with the full radial behavior of a quadratic. Indefiniteness alone does not preclude a star-shaped arbitrary quadratic sublevel set around another center (e.g. x²−y²≤1 about the origin). Neither the generic sufficiency argument nor the restricted wedge lemma gives the frozen necessity direction.

originality.rationale: The supported distinction is the necessity of Loewner order for visibility from the generating site under the full-space two-site assumptions, and thus its equivalence with convexity. The earlier work inspected treats site-star-shapedness as a hypothesis or supplies restricted and sufficient conditions, not this exact test. Two later-catalogued Resultary records do give the exact result in their overlapping scopes; that is direct mathematical coverage, not evidence that the finding was already covered at the time of this frozen record or a determination of provenance.
residual_risks: Broader quadratic-sublevel or anisotropic geometry literature may contain unlocated implications. The later exact overlaps do not establish who derived the criterion first, and the access limits do not prove absence of older coverage.

checked_sources: Venkovic–Anzt site-star hypothesis and Labelle–Shewchuk restricted visibility passages
value.rationale: The unrestricted two-site model is the smallest case in which heterogeneous site metrics can defeat visibility from a generating site. An exact matrix test distinguishes global visibility from potentially favorable clipped plots and distinguishes symmetric metric equality from one-sided dominance. Its useful content is the necessity direction and the resulting two-cell rigidity, not the routine sufficiency of convexity of a quadratic.
residual_risks: No implication for multisite diagrams, variable metrics, arbitrary star centers, or bounded observation windows is claimed.
